data.title: Palo Alto Networks (PANW) Stock Rallies After Q1 Earnings Revive Profit Story
data.description:
Palo Alto Networks just put Q1 2027 on the board with a sharp rebound in profitability, and traders wasted no time. The stock jumped 6.4% on Thursday to about US$361 after the release, a strong move for a large cybersecurity player.

That reaction hangs on one thing. Investors are cheering a swing from recent quarterly losses to Q1 net income of US$482 million on US$3.45b in revenue, and treating it as proof that the margin story is back on track. Whether that optimism matches the full set of numbers is where the real debate starts.

Q1 2027 Earnings Summary

  • Revenue (Q1 2027 vs. Q1 2026): US$3,445 million vs. US$2,474 million (up about 39% year over year based on management commentary)
  • Net Income (Excl. Extra Items, Q1 2027 vs. Q1 2026): US$482 million vs. US$334 million (higher profitability year over year)
  • Basic EPS (Q1 2027 vs. Q1 2026): US$0.59 vs. US$0.49 (earnings per share improved year over year)
  • Net Profit Margin (Trailing 12 Months vs. Prior Year): 3.7% vs. 11.7% (margin compressed over the last year)

Tired of scrolling through walls of earnings tables and raw figures? View Palo Alto Networks' full financial picture in clear charts, including how the valuation compares with its fundamentals, in our company report for Palo Alto Networks.

Palo Alto Networks’ Platform Ambition Meets Early Milestones

The bullish analyst narrative on Simply Wall St assumes Palo Alto Networks can turn AI driven platforms into a larger slice of security budgets.

"Bullish analysts expect Palo Alto Networks to compound its AI-driven security, identity, and observability platforms into a larger share of cybersecurity spending as customers consolidate onto its offerings."

Q1 results indicate that the consolidation story is not just talk. NGS ARR reached US$9.73b with 66% year over year growth, and net new NGS ARR more than doubled. Management reported a record 170 or so new platformizations and said platform customers now account for about two thirds of NGS ARR, with net retention above 120%. RPO of US$21.0b, up 35% year over year, provides additional evidence that multi year platform contracts are gaining traction.

One Narrative disagrees with today's price. → See where this Narrative says Palo Alto Networks should trade.

Palo Alto Networks Margins Face The Real Test

The bearish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St argues that Palo Alto Networks may see strong AI driven demand turn into weaker profit per dollar of revenue.

"Bearish analysts expect Palo Alto Networks to face sustained pressure on total gross margin as cloud hosting and hardware costs grow faster than revenue and weigh on profitability."

Q1 confirms part of that worry. Gross margin slipped to 75.2%, with management pointing to higher hardware components and a richer SaaS mix as the culprit. Yet non GAAP operating margin edged up to 30.7% and free cash flow margin reached 56%. Profitability held up this quarter, so the margin squeeze risk appears more like a forward concern than a problem already visible in earnings.

One essential aspect of assessing earnings quality is to look at how much a company is diluting shareholders. As it happens, Cha AI Healthcare issued 115% more new shares over the last year. Therefore, each share now receives a smaller portion of profit. To talk about net income, without noticing earnings per share, is to be distracted by the big numbers while ignoring the smaller numbers that talk to per share value. A Look At The Impact Of Cha AI Healthcare's Dilution On Its Earnings Per Share (EPS)

Three years ago, Cha AI Healthcare lost money. And even focusing only on the last twelve months, we don't have a meaningful growth rate because it made a loss a year ago, too. What we do know is that while it's great to see a profit over the last twelve months, that profit would have been better, on a per share basis, if the company hadn't needed to issue shares. And so, you can see quite clearly that dilution is having a rather significant impact on shareholders.

If Cha AI Healthcare's EPS can grow over time then that drastically improves the chances of the share price moving in the same direction. However, if its profit increases while its earnings per share stay flat (or even fall) then shareholders might not see much benefit. For that reason, you could say that EPS is more important that net income in the long run, assuming the goal is to assess whether a company's share price might grow.

Note: we always recommend investors check balance sheet strength. Click here to be taken to our balance sheet analysis of Cha AI Healthcare.

The Impact Of Unusual Items On Profit

On top of the dilution, we should also consider the ₩11b impact of unusual items in the last year, which had the effect of suppressing profit. While deductions due to unusual items are disappointing in the first instance, there is a silver lining. We looked at thousands of listed companies and found that unusual items are very often one-off in nature. And, after all, that's exactly what the accounting terminology implies. In the twelve months to September 2026, Cha AI Healthcare had a big unusual items expense. All else being equal, this would likely have the effect of making the statutory profit look worse than its underlying earnings power.

Our Take On Cha AI Healthcare's Profit Performance

To sum it all up, Cha AI Healthcare took a hit from unusual items which pushed its profit down; without that, it would have made more money. But unfortunately the dilution means that shareholders now own a smaller proportion of the company (assuming they maintained the same number of shares). That will weigh on earnings per share, even if it is not reflected in net income. Given the contrasting considerations, we don't have a strong view as to whether Cha AI Healthcare's profits are an apt reflection of its underlying potential for profit. data.title: Why Tokyo Kikai Seisakusho's (TSE:6335) Earnings Are Weaker Than They Seem
data.description:
Investors were disappointed with Tokyo Kikai Seisakusho, Ltd.'s (TSE:6335) recent earnings release. We did some digging and found some underlying numbers that are worrying.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Examining Cashflow Against Tokyo Kikai Seisakusho's Earnings

In high finance, the key ratio used to measure how well a company converts reported profits into free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio (from cashflow). The accrual ratio subtracts the FCF from the profit for a given period, and divides the result by the average operating assets of the company over that time. You could think of the accrual ratio from cashflow as the 'non-FCF profit ratio'.

Therefore, it's actually considered a good thing when a company has a negative accrual ratio, but a bad thing if its accrual ratio is positive. While having an accrual ratio above zero is of little concern, we do think it's worth noting when a company has a relatively high accrual ratio. Notably, there is some academic evidence that suggests that a high accrual ratio is a bad sign for near-term profits, generally speaking.

Over the twelve months to September 2026, Tokyo Kikai Seisakusho recorded an accrual ratio of 1.88. As a general rule, that bodes poorly for future profitability. To wit, the company did not generate one whit of free cashflow in that time. Even though it reported a profit of JP¥1.09b, a look at free cash flow indicates it actually burnt through JP¥669m in the last year. It's worth noting that Tokyo Kikai Seisakusho generated positive FCF of JP¥2.0b a year ago, so at least they've done it in the past. However, that's not all there is to consider. We can see that unusual items have impacted its statutory profit, and therefore the accrual ratio. One positive for Tokyo Kikai Seisakusho shareholders is that it's accrual ratio was significantly better last year, providing reason to believe that it may return to stronger cash conversion in the future. Shareholders should look for improved cashflow relative to profit in the current year, if that is indeed the case.

The Impact Of Unusual Items On Profit

Given the accrual ratio, it's not overly surprising that Tokyo Kikai Seisakusho's profit was boosted by unusual items worth JP¥474m in the last twelve months. data.title: This ASX Mining Stock Is Exploring A Critical Defence Mineral
data.description:
Modern defence systems don’t just run on technology. They depend on a range of critical minerals. Fighter jets, radar systems, precision weapons and ammunition all require specialised materials sourced from mines around the world. With global defence spending up 41% over the past decade, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI), securing reliable supplies of these materials is becoming increasingly important.

Two of these minerals are antimony and tungsten, two metals with important defence and industrial applications.

ASX small-cap mining stock, Red Mountain Mining (ASX:RMX), is looking to capitalise on this opportunity, with exploration projects targeting both minerals across Australia and the United States.

Why antimony and tungsten are critical minerals

Antimony and tungsten might not attract the same attention as gold, copper or rare earths, but both are important to modern defence and industrial manufacturing.

Antimony is used in lead alloys for ammunition, military batteries and explosives, as well as flame retardants and semiconductor components. Tungsten, meanwhile, is valued for its exceptional hardness, density and ability to withstand extremely high temperatures. These properties make it useful in armour-piercing ammunition, military equipment, jet engines and industrial cutting tools.

Both metals are recognised on Australia's Critical Minerals List, reflecting their importance to national security, advanced manufacturing and reliable global supply chains. They are also recognised as strategically important by key partners, including the US, UK, Japan, South Korea and the European Union.

However, securing reliable supplies is becoming increasingly important.

China dominates the supply of both metals, accounting for just over half of global antimony mine production, while Russia contributes around 29%. Its position is even stronger in tungsten, where China accounts for approximately 79% of global production.

This concentration leaves Western supply chains exposed to disruptions. China's past restrictions on critical mineral exports have reinforced the importance of developing alternative sources of supply, both domestically and among allied countries.

Antimony and tungsten’s growing demand

The growing demand for antimony and tungsten outside of China and Russia is starting to translate into real investment.

Antimony prices surged during 2024 and 2025, reaching around US$60,000 before retreating to approximately US$18,500. Despite the correction, prices remain above the levels seen before the supply squeeze.

Tungsten has experienced an even sharper rally. The price of ammonium paratungstate (APT), a processed intermediate product used in the tungsten supply chain, has risen by around 750% since January 2025.

As of January 2026, Australia has a pipeline of around 26 antimony projects at various stages of exploration, development and production. Several tungsten mines outside of China are also in various stages of development.

In Australia, Larvotto Resources (ASX: LRV) brought its Hillgrove antimony-gold project into production in 2026, targeting annual output of around 4,900 tonnes of antimony concentrate.

Meanwhile, the military demand for these minerals can be seen by Perpetua Resources (PPTA) securing up to US$40 million in funding from the US army to investigate tungsten production at its Stibnite project which also contains antimony. Also, United States Antimony (UAMY) has received US$12.8 million in US defence funding to expand its processing capacity.

Red Mountain delivering on antimony potential

Red Mountain’s Antimony-Gold Project in Armidale has seen encouraging signs from its maiden drilling program which included a 5 metre section containing an average of 5.2% antimony, which included a 3 metre section averaging 8.4%.

The results confirm that antimony-bearing rock extends beneath the surface, providing the first meaningful evidence of what may lie underground. However, further drilling will be needed to establish how extensive and consistent the mineralisation is.

The company plans to complete a drone-based magnetic survey by ;ate November which should help better understand the underground structures and identify where to drill next. Further drilling activities are planned in 2027.

Meanwhile, at Red Mountain’s Pioneer project in America, rock-chip samples have confirmed tungsten-bearing rock across several parts of the project.

What do investors think of this ASX mining stock?

The most-followed Red Mountain narrative on the Simply Wall St community sees the company as a speculative way to gain exposure to two strategically important metals. It points to the location of Armidale near Larvotto Resources’ Hillgrove project, as well as the company’s US antimony assets and its Pioneer Tungsten Project in Montana, which sits beside Almonty Industries’ project.

The narrative argues that these locations could give Red Mountain exposure to established mining districts and potential future demand for Western supply. However, it also acknowledges the company’s early exploration stage, lack of a resource estimate and ongoing funding requirements.

Red Mountain has exposure to two strategically important metals and some encouraging early exploration results. The challenge now is turning those early signs into defined resources. For investors, the next round of drilling will be far more important than the broader defence minerals story.
